question: If at same rate of interest, in 2 years, the simple interest is ₹42 and compound interest is ₹51, then what is the principal (in ₹)?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

SI for 1 year = 42 ÷ 2 = ₹21

CI − SI difference for 2 years = 51 − 42 = ₹9

Rate % = (Difference ÷ 1st year SI) × 100 = (9 ÷ 21) × 100 = 300/7%

Principal = (1st year SI × 100) ÷ Rate %

Principal = (21 × 100) ÷ (300/7) = 21 × 7/3 = ₹49

**∴ The correct answer is ₹49.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Simple Interest (SI) for 2 years = ₹42

Compound Interest (CI) for 2 years = ₹51

**Formula Used:**

SI for 1 year = Total SI ÷ Time

Difference (CI − SI) for 2 years = Interest on first year's SI
